intro: Keyword and vector search often find different useful documents. Their raw scores are not directly comparable, but their ranks can be combined.
task: Return document IDs sorted by weighted reciprocal rank fusion score: sum(weight / (rank_constant + rank)) across lists.
requirements: rankings is a list of lists of string IDs. Deduplicate each list in order before assigning one-based ranks.
rank_constant must be a positive finite numeric scalar, excluding booleans. Default weights are all 1.
Optional weights must match the number of lists, be finite and nonnegative, and contain a positive value unless there are no lists.

Break score ties by ascending document ID. limit is None or a nonnegative integer (not bool); larger limits simply return every document. Leave inputs unchanged and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Deduplicate each list
hints.body: Each document can contribute at most once per retrieval method.

hints.title: Accumulate rank contributions
hints.body: For each one-based rank, add that list's weight divided by constant plus rank.

hints.title: Sort deterministically
hints.body: Sort by negative accumulated score and then by the document ID.

explanation: Reciprocal rank fusion uses positions rather than raw retrieval scores. This avoids pretending that cosine and keyword scores share a scale.
The rank constant controls how sharply early positions dominate. Larger values flatten the differences among nearby ranks.
Fusion is a hypothesis to evaluate, not a guaranteed improvement. Compare against each baseline on held-out queries and inspect individual misses.
